links.outcome: Extraction accuracy of LLM-based versus ontology-driven platform on same pathology reports
links.effect: Brim mean 96.7% pancreatic; T stage 96.4% vs DeepPhe 83.6% pancreatic and 70.6% breast; N stage comparable (96.4% pancreatic, 94.1% breast for DeepPhe).
links.quote: DeepPhe performed comparably for N stage (96.4% pancreatic, 94.1% breast) but had notable T stage deficits (83.6% pancreatic, 70.6% breast).

links.outcome: Accuracy of tool on local hospital data across cancer types
links.effect: Brim mean 96.7% on pancreatic, with a 3.0 p.p. decline on breast cancer (mean 93.7%).
links.quote: Brim Analytics achieved high accuracy across seven registry variables in pancreatic cancer (mean 96.7%), including T stage (96.4%) and histologic grade (97.0%), with a 3.0 p.p. decline on breast cancer (mean 93.7%).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation comparing an LLM-based data abstraction platform against an ontology-driven NLP system on pathology reports from a hospital dataset without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
